description: REQ-AS-001's explicit EARS edge case ('Registry file present but empty slots: []: loop body runs zero times, exits 0 cleanly') is not covered by any test. test_earning_health_allslots.sh's section (C) tests a MISSING registry FILE (EARNHC_REGISTRY pointing at a path that does not exist), not a PRESENT, valid, well-formed registry whose `slots` array is empty -- a materially different code path (the `[ ! -f "$REGISTRY" ]` early-exit at earning-health-allslots.sh:31-34 vs. the python row-extraction + while-loop-over-zero-rows path at lines 39-110). Static trace-through of the script suggests the empty-array path does exit 0 cleanly, but this is unverified by any actual test run, and is exactly the kind of edge case REQ-AS-001 explicitly calls out as needing to 'never crash a launchd tick.'

evidence.snippet:
echo "(C) missing registry file -> no-op, never crashes"
D2="$(mktemp -d)"
OUT3="$(EARNHC_REGISTRY="$D2/missing-registry.json" ... bash "$SCRIPT" ...)"
a "missing registry logs and exits cleanly" "$OUT3" "no registry at"
